title: The Secure Bond: The Emotional Foundation for Every Future Learning
summary: Attachment theory (Bowlby/Ainsworth) is established: a child who feels secure with a responsive parent develops a 'secure base' from which to explore the world with confidence. Consistent response to crying, eye contact, mutual smiling, and physical presence—these build an 'internal working model' of self-worth and trust in others. The 'Early Moments Matter' report (UNICEF) states: the first three years are a critical period for brain development. According to Harvard's Center on the Developing Child, responsive back-and-forth interaction between a child and a caring adult builds the neural connections in the child's brain, while chronic neglect can cause 'toxic stress' that harms brain development, learning and health for years. If you notice no responsive smiling or following of faces and voices, or a clear delay in interaction and movement, see your paediatrician or a child development specialist.
try_this: Today: when your child cries or calls you, respond warmly and as promptly as you can, even with a word: 'I'm coming, my love.' In the first months you cannot spoil a baby with attention. Start with his most pressing need: is he hungry, cold, tired or in pain, or does his nappy need changing? Notice: does he settle when you respond?
reflection_prompts: How did you experience ease or anxiety as a parent? Do you see its impact on how you interact with your child?
What moment did you feel your child 'trusts' you completely?
